reviews.title: Somehow cluttered and empty at the same time
reviews.text:
Pros:
--it's pretty and it can be played without spending a single penny.
Cons:
--I hit the level cap and progress on all aspects of the game just stopped. I finally deleted the app when it became a daily repetition of just doing the same thing and making no progress. I hit the level cap, and though you can upgrade armor/weapon pieces beyond that, it was clear even that little bit wasn't going to be enough.
--Do you like currencies? There's approximately fifteen million different kinds of currencies to level up and upgrade things. Two different kinds of leveling up and they both take three or four different kinds of currency. Upgrading armor? There's six kinds of materials, each with their own levels, for that. It's absurd and confusing. Your inventory will be full of hundreds of different items that only have one use and will sit there until you have enough of them to use. And depending on when events roll around, that could take awhile.
--The characters are poorly balanced. There's a whole group of fighters that exist only to be disposed of (to create more of one of the seven thousand kinds of currencies). The newer flashier characters are given better stats. Older ones get ignored. You can equip two similar characters with the same items and get one that is clearly superior.
--The devs have ignored parts of the game in favor of events and activities that are just PVP arena variations. There was an area  that involved moving around a grid and using strategy and puzzle-solving mechanics that I quite enjoyed but once I got through the twenty or so levels of that, they never added anything to it, despite a "coming soon..." note at the end.
--Story? If there's a story it's buried so deep I couldn't find it. There's snippets of plot here and there but they're all just vague sci-fi themed non-sequiturs without any context to connect them or be engaging in any way. There's three factions: one that's a human society with advanced tech and robotics, one that's a mishmash of fantasy-themed monster-folk, and one super-sci-fi alien race that's trying really hard to be Warframe without triggering a copyright issue. Are these three factions at war with each other, are they cooperating in some kind of alliance? Who cares, look at the pretty designs and cool animation, pay no attention to the lack of substance!
------ having said all that, I did plug along for way longer that I probably should have before finally just deleting the app. I tried to delete my account altogether but there seems to be no way to do that. Least of this game's problems, really.
But hey, it's pretty.

reviews.title: Not fun anymore.
reviews.text:
Game used to be fun, balanced, game has become imbalanced, horrible monetization from someone who spend a good amount of money on the game. If you are not spending thousands of dollars….you wont be in the top of rankings. They no longer have pve events…even the ones that are disguised as pve are pvp events…..and don’t expect to clear all the rewards. They expect u to have specific characters to do major events but wont give you trial characters like Honkai Star Rail or Wuthering Waves to help the community get all the rewards…dungeons are extremely hard to clear….game keeps updating at an accelerated pace….u invest in a hero…next month they are obsolete.  Awakening system if horrible because they will have an awakening hero that has zero synergy with the current playing team and they release an awakening every 3 weeks. They have a ton of different summoning currency in the game but won’t update the shops to add old heroes to obtain, new summoning currency. The scam SP heroes are $3000 plus to max out and if you don’t spend it will take years to max on out. 

Guild events are way too frequent. I was in a strong and fun guild but when they made the guild events back to back, I was having an issue sleeping properly just to help the guild out with hitting bosses. Quitting the game was the best thing a did for my health, I get more sleep, I don’t have to be logging in multiple times in a game, I don’t have to be constantly checking discord. Dailies take 1 hour and 40 minutes to complete for an idle game….thats if you hitting all the bosses, doing guild stuff and also pve/pvp events…They also add skip function where it’s not needed…eg twilight lands and exotic expedition and if you skip and lose or even win….you lose the characters that die…talk about a scummy company. 

They use to have the new prototypes go to Twilight lands after a few weeks but no longer do so and they have another currency to make prototypes better but it’s random what u get. I’m not sure if the wishlist is 10 prototypes crystal…..that’s just ridiculous….a selector summon would have been so much better. That’s if u can get the prototypes in the first place. 

The prototypes accurately account for significant stat boost for your team and if u don’t spend….u don’t be able to make it in the Ascension Arena.  

I think they gave up on the game and are milking saw much as they can from those who still play until the game EOS. 

Revenue of the game also keeps dropping because people are realizing how scummy the develops are. I don’t think this game will last a year from now.

reviews.title: After about a year- I’m done.
reviews.text:
When I first started playing, it was a lot of fun- decent depth, lots of build crafting. 

But, after that sheen wore off, this game just became a tedious slog. Lots of the game becoming unplayable unless I invested in heroes I didn’t like (oooo, a Scantily Clad Succubus, how quaint) or was unwilling to pay for (SP Heroes, good luck getting Conner unless you’ve got loads of discretionary income). PvP being largely unapproachable for the light spender. And, just… Boring after a while (especially that lame joke card game).

A lot of the interesting social media content providers just stopping covering this game. If it’s not enough to keep them engaged (& they get benefits for doing it) then how do they expect to keep anyone else engaged?

So, yeah, fun, but shows its colors (P2W) real quick.

reviews.title: Predatory. Ultra P2W.  Don’t bother.
reviews.text:
Out of all the gatcha games I played in the last 5-6 years this is by far the most P2W and predatory.   They have a $199.99 bundle in their store. That should tell you everything.  You can’t even use gems to get the better (SSS) heroes. You have to buy bundles that have tickets for those pulls. The only things you can pull for are pretty basic crap heroes. And there’s something like 5 or 6 evolutions each needing the same (in increasing quantities) copy of that 0.14% Chance to pull here (ONLY with bought tickets and not gems). It’s absurd how predatory this game is. Even the honeymoon period compared to other games - that load you with items and heroes to make you think it’ll always be like that so you start buying things - is awful. 

Stay away. There’s better games to lose your money on.

reviews.title: Awesome Game
reviews.text:
This game is great. There's no "energy cap" that only let's you play for a certain amount of time, you can play until you lose (which doesn't happen.) There is absolutely 0 pay to play, the game gives everything you need to progress out like candy. I've only been playing for maybe 5 days and already have a bunch of epics, a mythic, and a thousand legendary heroes. The only reason to invest money into the game is to support the developers, which I highly encourage to get another great game. There's a million things to do in the game; there's the main story, side story, past story, exploration type missions, etc..and all of them give you a ton of rewards. The game looks phenomenal, and is very easy to follow. 
Usually not a fan of this type of game, but I saw the ad and tried it. Haven't been able to put it down. There's just so many things they got right. I've never left a review on a game but this game is really great so I wanted to share. Thanks for making it how you did!

reviews.title: They will steal your money
reviews.text: I actually really enjoy this game, and so I have spent money on it. That being said, I believe EE knows this, so they ended up charging me for something that I did not buy; in speaking with their customer service, if you can call it that, they attributed it to a past purchase. Simply not true, as I have banks statements that do not match their claim. They then said it was a delay from Apple sending me the receipt, also not true, as I have the past receipt from Apple. I was refunded the purchase by Apple, and EE banned my account, telling me to open a new one and spending the same amount of money to unban my account (all for a purchase I never made). I believe they recognize when which players tend to pay money towards their game, and (judging from other reviews) they will phantom charge or double/triple charge these players, knowing that they spend a fair amount of time and money on the game and will do what it takes to unban their account, and then when questioned about it, they give the run around. This game should, at the very least, have a warning in the App Store that it has a history of fraudulent activity
